This establishes local I/O ownership, but does not independently prove Safety membership or final safety-function semantics.

Word 1006 is in active Configio and safety-model evidence records the resolver-derived local endpoint.

evidence_used: Cluster deterministic code ENDPOINT_ON_ACTIVE_CONTROLLER for ESPB24 and ESPB2.
PhysicalWordResolver evidence resolves ESPB24 word 1001 bit 7 to AENTR1:I.DATA[3].7.
PhysicalWordResolver evidence resolves ESPB2 word 1006 bit 14 to AENTR3:I.DATA[4].4.
Words 1001 and 1006 are present in the MSCRENOPICK active Configio word sample.
Conveyor named claims identify MSCRENOPICK as source machine for both devices.
Safety-model evidence union associates each word/bit with its resolver-derived endpoint, although its final status remains REVIEW_REQUIRED.
why_alternatives_rejected: ENGINEER_CONFIRM_REQUIRED is not the preferred ownership result because active-controller word presence plus resolver-derived local endpoints provide sufficient derived evidence of local ownership; engineering confirmation remains appropriate only for safety semantics or hardware validation.
FOREIGN_CONTROLLER lacks cited evidence of another controller, remote owner, or foreign binding; the available evidence instead points to MSCRENOPICK.
INTERNAL_LOGICAL is inconsistent with resolver-derived module input endpoints and active Configio word membership.
SPARE_UNUSED is unsupported because both points have named conveyor/safety-related references and resolved input endpoints.
response.recommended_action: Accept the cluster as LOCAL MSCRENOPICK IO ownership and add the two resolved endpoints to the physical_io_map with derived provenance. Do not mark either point as a Safety member or assign safety-function behavior solely from this resolution.
additional_evidence_needed: Authoritative MSCRENOPICK I/O hardware/configuration export confirming AENTR1 slot 3 and AENTR3 slot 4 channel assignments.
Controlled safety configuration or approved electrical documentation if Safety membership, E-stop function, or criticality must be asserted.
Source-level mapping reconciliation for Conveyor.asc, EStop.asc, and Errors.asc, whose current final statuses remain REVIEW_REQUIRED.

ESPB32 (1143.0) has resolved endpoint AENTR2:I.DATA[3].0, with deterministic code ENDPOINT_ON_ACTIVE_CONTROLLER and reason that a local endpoint is proven via PhysicalWordResolver.
Both devices are MSCRENOPICK claims in FORTNA/Conveyor.asc and have corroborating safety-model evidence, although those source records remain REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Both devices share module AENTR2 and adjacent active input words, supporting a single cluster-level local remote-I/O conclusion.

INTERNAL_LOGICAL if authoritative configuration evidence shows the AENTR2 endpoint resolutions are aliases rather than physical remote-I/O bindings.
why_alternatives_rejected: ENGINEER_CONFIRM_REQUIRED is more conservative but is not the best current classification because active Configio membership plus two independently resolved AENTR2 input endpoints provides affirmative local-binding evidence.

UNSUPPORTED is not appropriate because words, module, slots, directions, and endpoints are all evidenced.
